title: EXP-031 — Select Form Retained-Filter Refresh Semantics
objective: In one read-only experiment against the existing live Web Client, characterize whether the Select Form dialog applies a retained exact Name filter when the dialog is ordinarily cancelled and reopened. First use known-existing `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02` as the positive control: with Filter By=Name and Case Sensitive unchecked, set that exact filter, ordinarily Cancel the dialog, reopen Select Form once, and verify whether the reopened settled rendered grid contains the expected exact row. Then use a deliberately uncreated FX_-prefixed absence probe `FX_SelectFormFilterProbe01`: set that exact filter, ordinarily Cancel, reopen Select Form once, and verify whether the reopened settled rendered grid shows zero visible case-insensitive Name matches. Record any corresponding supported request/response evidence only as corroboration; rendered settled rows are the semantic evidence. This experiment is read-only and must not create, save, change, close, or reopen any Designer Form.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence proves a usable live Web Client Select Form workflow, preserves all inherited Designer/Web Client Form state untouched, and records that no Mongoose artifact mutation, Save, Regenerate, unload, preference change, or session-establishment action occurred.

Positive-control evidence shows Filter By=Name, Case Sensitive visibly unchecked, and exact filter `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02` before ordinary Cancel; after exactly one fresh Select Form reopen, the settled rendered result visibly contains the expected exact `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab02` row. If the reopened result is stale or ambiguous after the bounded inspection, this check fails.

Absence-probe evidence shows Filter By=Name, Case Sensitive visibly unchecked, and exact filter `FX_SelectFormFilterProbe01` before ordinary Cancel; after exactly one fresh Select Form reopen, the settled rendered result visibly contains zero case-insensitive Name matches for that probe. The result is classified only as zero visible matches in this inspected refreshed Select Form result, not database absence.

Evidence reconciles exactly two tested filter/reopen sequences: one known-present positive control and one uncreated FX_-prefixed absence probe, with no additional Select Form lifecycle retries beyond the explicitly bounded recovery allowance.

Final repository and action audit proves changes are confined to the EXP-031 record plus `evidence/EXP-031/`, no Mongoose artifacts were created or modified, and the resulting finding is limited to Select Form retained-filter/reopen behavior in the tested 2026.09.08 environment.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261007-195234-KQJh. Rationale: EXP-030 was blocked before mutation because changing the Select Form filter text in an already-open dialog left stale rendered rows, and the one bounded refill inspection produced no refresh. Rather than retry or repair EXP-030, the smallest useful next learning step is a separate read-only experiment that explicitly tests the different supported dialog-lifecycle approach already observed in successful preflights such as EXP-028: dismiss Select Form normally, reopen it, and determine whether a retained exact Name filter is applied to a newly populated rendered result. Establishing this UI behavior independently would give the factory a verified preflight primitive without making any claim about EXP-030 or any Form/component recovery behavior.
